3DCodeVerse: How to Code Your Own 3D Universe  
  
Build a realistic 3D world without ever touching a modeling tool. The project named 3D Code Verse gives coding agents a complete workshop where they can write, run, and fix the actual scripts that make objects, scenes, and graphics come alive. Instead of guessing at images, these programs are measured against real physics and rendered views, so the system knows exactly when a joint is broken or a light is flat. It then repairs the code automatically, turning every failure into better training data for the next model. This turns 3D creation from a black box into a transparent, code-based workflow you can actually inspect and improve.  
  
Open source: gaoypeng/3dcodeverse

The result is built and executed. Failures return build or runtime feedback. Otherwise spatial tools measure properties such as dimensions, contact, collision, placement, and articulation. A vision-language-model judge, which evaluates images and text together, then inspects multi-view renders against the request and acceptance criteria. Findings are prioritized into targeted repair tasks, and a fix agent revises the code. Measured violations can cap a score or veto visual claims the measurements contradict, so geometry checks and visual judgment work together rather than substituting for each other.

Schematic of the 3DCodeVerse harness from planning through build, judging, repair, and scored rounds [...] View Paper

## AI Overview

Getting 3D code to run is the easy part. A script can build without errors and still yield an asset with missing, misplaced, or colliding parts, and fixing those defects by hand does not scale. 3DCodeVerse, the system described in this paper, hands the checking and repair to agents that plan, build, measure, render, judge, and revise the code with no human steering the revisions. The authors argue that this loop is what makes high-quality 3D programs achievable without human feedback.

The clearest payoff is a controlled comparison. On a 60-prompt set of 3D objects, the same Claude Opus 5.5 backbone was preferred 90% of the time when run inside the 3DCodeVerse harness versus inside Claude Design. [...] ## A corpus of runnable 3D

Code-authored 3D assets are editable and executable, but the data and tools for making them have been scattered across tasks and environments. 3DCodeVerse tries to supply shared infrastructure, including automated corpus construction. The corpus spans static objects, articulated objects, scenes, and graphics.

The headline scale needs care. 3DCodeVerse-2M's roughly 2.03 million refers to code–condition pairs and export rows, not unique programs; the catalogue indexes 269,597 unique executable programs. Verification coverage varies by source, so not every item received the same geometric and visual checks as the harness-generated ones.
